mentl/c4164a5:
Two substrate primitives, both non-deployed but useful:

(1) $buf_contains in buffer.wat — linear-search membership probe over
    Buffer<A>. Makes Buffer<A> usable as a visited-set (DAG-aware
    walks, oracle-cached subscription, etc.). Currently linear; named
    peer Hβ.runtime.buffer-hashset for O(log N) sorted-insert
    or O(1) hash-keyed variant once wheel-scale fn count grows past
    the linear-acceptable threshold.

(2) list_extend_to heap-top in-place trick in list.wat — when
    align(list_end) == heap_ptr (the list is at the most-recent
    allocation), grow it via $perm_alloc instead of fresh make_list +
    copy. Canonical bump-allocator zone-realloc trick (GMP / glibc /
    V8). Amortized O(1) per push for buffer-counter callers in
    infer/lower that haven't yet migrated to Buffer<A>. Named peer
    Hβ.runtime.buffer-substrate-adoption for the migration.

Both are SUBSTRATE primitives — they exist; deployment is per-caller.
Buffer<A>-as-visited-set was attempted in cfn_walk + emit_functions
this session but the linear $buf_contains was wheel-scale-prohibitive,
AND the underlying issue surfaced wasn't actually pointer-sharing
(DAG dedup) but NAME collision at handler-arm fn naming —
multiple handlers' $op_yield arms emit duplicate (func) declarations,
each with unique LowFn pointers but colliding names. The right fix
is at the lower-stage where LowFn names are minted, not at the
emit-stage walk.

Cursor of attention: Hβ.first-light.handler-arm-fn-name-discriminator
— extend $lower_handler_arms_as_decls (seed + wheel) to mint
$op_<handler_name>_<op_name> (or a structural-handle discriminator)
so each handler arm gets a unique WASM symbol. This IS the H1.4
named follow-up at src/lower.nx:790-794 ("Single-handler-per-op
naming for now").

two-top/c4d030a:
An online match decided on score now produces a proof. Each install
mints an ed25519 keypair beside its install-id (profile.json, hex);
pubkeys ride a new Profile2 side-channel message next to the legacy
Profile, so a mixed pairing degrades to unsigned results instead of
breaking. On MatchOver with the threshold reached, both peers
serialize one canonical net::MatchStatement — seats sorted by
install-id, the sorted matchbox peer-id pair as the session nonce, a
per-session match index so RUN IT BACK repeats stay distinct — sign
it, and swap signatures on the reliable channel. When the peer's
signature verifies and the recorder freezes the tape,
<stem>.attest.json lands beside it and the rival's ledger line gains
an attested_wins credit.

replay_sync --attest <tape> <attest.json> is the verifier: re-run the
tape, rebuild the statement from what the sim actually produced,
check both signatures against the pubkeys inside the statement. The
test suite's decided tape is built the honest way — loop the
canonical choreography, probe for the deciding tick, truncate with a
neutral tail, because apply_rematch restarts on a THROW edge from
either player and a tape that keeps pressing past the decision
re-simulates into a fresh 0-0.

Forfeits stay ledger-only: each client's lobby FSM observes the
walk-away at its own frame, so there is no shared statement to sign.
ed25519-dalek is pinned =2.2.0; the 3.0 major stays out until it has
evidence behind it.
